questions.prompt: How many official stops are on the Freedom Trail?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: Sixteen. Sixteen places where history happened. Most tourists quit after ten. Sully walked all sixteen every year. Called it 'paying respects.'
questions.npcReactionWrong: Sixteen. You've walked the Freedom Trail, right? Most people don't finish it.

questions.prompt: Faneuil Hall has been called 'The Cradle of Liberty.' What was its original purpose when built in 1742?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: A marketplace. Meat, produce, goods. The upstairs was for town meetings. Liberty came later. Commerce came first. Always does.
questions.npcReactionWrong: A marketplace. Ground floor was markets, upstairs was public meetings. Peter Faneuil funded it.

questions.prompt: The Boston Massacre occurred in 1770 outside what building?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: Outside the Old State House. King Street. March 5, 1770. Crispus Attucks was the first to fall. First martyr of the Revolution.
questions.npcReactionWrong: The Old State House. Five colonists died. State Street now, used to be King Street.

questions.prompt: What symbol sits atop Faneuil Hall, and what does it represent?
choices: A codfish - symbol of the fishing industry
A whale - symbol of maritime trade
questions.npcReactionCorrect: A grasshopper. Weathervane. Shem Drowne made it in 1742. During the Revolution, they used it to test if someone was a real Bostonian or a British spy.
questions.npcReactionWrong: A grasshopper. Look at the top of Faneuil Hall. Most people don't notice. It's been there since 1742.

questions.prompt: The Old North Church, where signal lanterns were hung, is located in which Boston neighborhood?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: North End. Christ Church, most people call it Old North Church. Still standing. Still active. You can visit any Sunday.
questions.npcReactionWrong: North End. One if by land, two if by sea. Everyone knows the poem, not everyone knows where the church is.

alternateQuestions.prompt: Boston Common is the oldest public park in the United States. What year was it established?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: 1634. Boston Common's been public land longer than America's been a country. Think about that.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: 1634. The oldest public park in America. Before the Pilgrims' grandchildren were born.

alternateQuestions.prompt: What cemetery along the Freedom Trail contains the graves of Paul Revere, Samuel Adams, and John Hancock?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: Granary Burying Ground. Revere, Adams, Hancock—all buried in the same place. Patriots' Row.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: Granary Burying Ground. The who's who of the Revolution, all in one cemetery.

alternateQuestions.prompt: What was dumped into Boston Harbor during the Tea Party, and how many chests?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: 342 chests. British East India Company tea. Dumped in the harbor. Worth a fortune then. Worth more now as a symbol.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: 342 chests of tea. The Tea Party threw cargo overboard. Exactly how much? 342 chests.

alternateQuestions.prompt: The Old South Meeting House was the starting point for what famous event?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: The Tea Party. December 16, 1773. Colonists gathered there, got angry, marched to the harbor. The rest is history.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: Old South Meeting House is famous for one night. The Tea Party started there before they marched to the harbor.

alternateQuestions.prompt: What is the name of the marketplace complex adjacent to Faneuil Hall?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: Quincy Market. Faneuil Hall's just one building. The big market hall next door is Quincy Market. Named for Mayor Josiah Quincy.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: Quincy Market. People confuse them all the time. Faneuil Hall is the historic building. Quincy Market is the long hall.

redemptionChallenge.instructions: Identify 5 of 7 Freedom Trail stops from photographs.
redemptionChallenge.npcPassResponse: Not bad. Most tourists can't tell one old building from another. Sully would've named all sixteen sites, the years they were built, and who died there.
redemptionChallenge.npcFailResponse: You thought that was the State House? That was Faneuil Hall! The crowd has spoken. They want you to try again.
